claimCounting: 69 inventoried lesson propositions;18 integrated question reviews including all prompts/options/keys/worked examples;36 glossary definitions/aliases;12 analogy mapping/limit reviews. No formula blocks. Repeated prose is not counted twice.
corrections: Integration pseudocode had independent completion and deadline branches, allowing two terminal outcomes despite the prose prohibition. It now resolves one SAMPLE/FAILED/TIMEOUT outcome inside an active attempt and ends it exactly once.

A disappearing fault was called evidence that timing changed. Logging can affect memory use as well. The lesson now says to investigate timing or memory effects rather than infer a particular cause or a repaired defect.
Host debugger source-variable inspection lacked its debug-information prerequisite. Added the prerequisite and a direct primary optimisation/debugging reference.
Task stack was aliased to an RTOS task (an execution context), rather than stack memory. Removed that alias and added a precise independently sourced Task stack entry; glossary grows35→36.

Instrumentation/logging pointed to watchpoint docs; testing/fake/boundary concepts pointed only at the C standard; time sharing pointed only at a task header; device ownership pointed only at queues; recovery image pointed only at SDK README. Replaced these with fetched primary logging, test/fake, scheduler, semaphore/resource and actual board workflow references, and corrected the logging question link.

Seven definitions describing the course’s own health/recovery/adapter policies carried unrelated vendor/C-standard URLs that do not define those policies. Removed those misleading external source fields; the verification record explicitly traces them to stated lesson requirements, the executed formal host model and independent adapter/health traces. They are not asserted to be SDK/ISO guarantees.

Automatic links captured ordinary application readings as IEEE normal numbers/audio samples, host model state as a virtualization host-state area, loop waiting as loop tiling, queue policy as access policy, C test conditions as electronics measurements and driver failure results as errno. Rephrased those occurrences without changing question IDs, keys or application requirements.

The rendered official Debug Probe site fetched in the browser but returned HTTP403 to the direct link checker. Replaced its glossary/reference URL with the fetched canonical Raspberry Pi documentation source.
gaps: No physical board, sensor, output wiring, watchdog, reset circuitry, timing instrument or actual FreeRTOS port executed. Host tests establish exercised policy, not target timing/electrical reliability.

Board adapter remains clearly labelled integration pseudocode. Choosing a real board/sensor still requires documented acquisition/decoding/timeout resolution/output mapping and separate hardware observations.
Health/degraded-operation policy is a deliberately constructed course example; no general safety, timing or recovery guarantee is inferred from a watchdog refresh.
Advanced bootloaders, updates, power characterization, production recovery, safety certification and full timing proof remain outside the introductory brief.

esr-debugging-observation: Input decoding, state transition and physical output require different evidence.
Breakpoint stops at a selected execution location; watchpoint can stop on value change.
Hardware watchpoints have target-specific support/limits; software watchpoints add overhead.
Optimisation affects variables and source mapping; suitable debug information is needed.
Host debugging differs from target probe/connection/configuration.
Logging adds execution/storage costs and can alter observed behavior without repairing a defect.
Logs/ISR work require bounded rate and capacity.
Halting changes external interactions and deadlines; external equipment need not pause.
Single-hypothesis observations and state/event/timestamp/failure result traces are an explicit debugging method.
esr-test-without-board: Deterministic logic can be separated from device electrical/timing dependencies.
Fictional application contract valid0–100, normalbelow70, alert70–100, invalidoutside.
C relational expressions yield int zero or one.
Enabled assert diagnoses failure and aborts; NDEBUG suppresses the checks.
Assertions are test expectations, not production sensor-failure policy.
Actual complete C11 program outputs logic checks passed.
Threshold neighbours69/70 and validity endpoints distinguish specified rules.
Controlled fake dependencies can supply repeatable normal/failure/timeout inputs.
Substituting a valid reading for missing acquisition hides failure.
Host tests validate exercised logic but not target registers, interrupts, electrical compatibility or timing.
Boundary tests and state transitions need explicit expected results.
esr-watchdog-reset: Timeout bounds one operation; watchdog supervises chosen progress and configured recovery.
Hardware countdown requires refresh to avoid expiry; clocks/reset coverage/limits vary.
Chosen supervisor policy requires current loop/acquisition/status progress.
Handled timeout can be progress under explicit degraded-operation policy, not healthy sensor evidence.
Periodic ISR refresh can hide a stalled main loop.
Stale earlier-window flags are not current progress evidence.
Reset cause must be interpreted using device boot documentation before relevant evidence changes.
Outputs and application start state require deliberate initialization.
Course reset returnsWAITING; timeout latchesFAULT; recovery does not reuse staleNORMAL.
Persistent resets need observable diagnostics and recovery rather than hiding a reboot loop.
Official hardware watchdog example exists; debug pause differs from normal workload.
Host model checks policy but cannot validate watchdog clock/reset hardware.
esr-rtos-when: Bounded cooperative loops can meet small application requirements without an RTOS.
RTOS organizes tasks/waiting but cannot cure unbounded work or overload by installation.
Task has execution state and its own finite stack.
One core executes at most one task at an instant; ready/running/blocked distinctions matter.
Higher-priority ready work can preempt lower-priority task under stated enabled configuration.
Blocked sensor permits ready logger; becomingready permits preemption; laterblocking permitslogger.
Deadline guarantees require workload/interference/resource bounds beyond priority.
Shared peripheral access requires ownership/protection; arbitrary drivers are not automatically concurrent-safe.
Queue capacity/full-buffer policy and task stack budget remain explicit requirements.
Adding tasks has configuration/debugging/resource costs, justified by concrete coordination benefit.
esr-sensor-state-machine: SAMPLE/TIMEOUT/FAILED/RESET are explicit application event labels, not automatic physical actions.
Valid range0–100 and threshold70 are fictional application requirements.
Reset has precedence and returnsWAITING from any modeled state.
FAULT remains latched for every nonreset event, including a valid sample.
States name software indication policy, not electrical pin levels.
C enum names integer alternatives; conditional selects only the chosen result expression.
Actual step has bounded comparisons, no loop/recursion/device wait.
Complete actual host C11 model outputs project checks passed and checks11 state transitions.
Adapter must acquire, decode, bound wait and map state to actual documented indicator/status.
Host simulation does not validate sensor accuracy, electrical interface, hardware timeout or complete target firmware.
esr-project-workflow: Exact displayed C11 compile/run command succeeds with assertions enabled.
Shell backslash continuation and output naming are correct under stated compiler option support.
Warnings/pass cases provide scoped evidence, not all-input or target-timing proof.
Six listed acceptance outcomes agree with explicit model, including latching/recovery.
Integration uses exact supported low-voltage board/SDK/pin/power limits and onboard indicator.
Unknown external/high-current/mains/inductive loads are excluded from direct MCU pin connection.
Pseudocode is integration policy, not a runnable universal SDK.
One active read attempt must end with exactly one chosen terminal outcome.
Simultaneous completion/deadline needs documented driver/timing resolution, not duplicate dispatch.
Read failure cannot cause endless blocking retries; other loop work remains bounded.
Actual flash/observation/reset/recovery tests are separate from host model and use safe fakes where needed.
Known-good image and official flash/debug route provide a chosen recovery baseline, not universal reliability.

esr-debugging-observation.rationale: Added delivery investigation: different observations answer different causal questions; explicit limitation covers processor halts and logging costs changing behavior. All debugging facts remain visible.

esr-test-without-board.rationale: Added cue-card rehearsal: chosen repeatable inputs test decisions; explicit limitation excludes physical sensor/clock/electrical integration evidence. No test expectations depend on the story.

esr-watchdog-reset.rationale: Added scheduled check-in: refresh is current progress evidence under a defined policy; limit correctly rejects reset as wiring repair or proof of software correctness.

esr-rtos-when.rationale: Added shared workshop bench: ready jobs compete for a single resource while blocked jobs step aside; limit retains exact scheduler/interference/resource/deadline concerns. Not an RTOS timing proof.

esr-sensor-state-machine.rationale: Added parcel inspection: input validation and indication are software policy with fault latching; limit excludes hardware accuracy/timing and safety certification. Recovery remains explicit in visible model.

esr-project-workflow.rationale: Added rehearsal then venue check: repeatable model tests and actual integration provide different scoped evidence; limit explicitly rejects general reliability or worst-case timing guarantees.
